name: Argentina
known: Football, and the legacy of Diego Maradona and Lionel Messi
Tango, beef and Malbec wine
Patagonia, glaciers and the Andes
facts: The second-largest country in South America by area, after Brazil.
Aconcagua, near the Chilean border, is the highest mountain outside Asia at about 6,960 metres.
The capital, Buenos Aires, is one of the largest cities in South America.

name: Brazil
known: Football and Carnival
The Amazon rainforest
Exports of soybeans, coffee, iron ore and beef
Beaches and the city of Rio de Janeiro
facts: The largest country in South America, and the only one where Portuguese is the main language.
Most of the Amazon rainforest lies inside Brazil.
The capital, Brasília, was built from scratch and opened in 1960; the biggest city is São Paulo.

name: Canada
known: Ice hockey, maple syrup and cold winters
The Rocky Mountains, Niagara Falls and huge areas of wilderness
Oil, timber and mining
A reputation for welcoming immigrants and international students, though study permits are now capped
facts: The second-largest country in the world by area.
English and French are both official languages of the federal government; Quebec is mainly French-speaking.
It has ten provinces and three territories, and most people live in cities in the south, near the border with the United States.

name: Chile
known: Copper, of which it is the world's largest producer
Wine, fruit and salmon exports
The Atacama Desert and the Andes
Easter Island (Rapa Nui)
facts: It is about 4,300 kilometres long but rarely more than 200 kilometres wide.
The Atacama is one of the driest places on Earth, and its clear skies make it a home for major telescopes.
The capital is Santiago, where more than a third of Chileans live.

name: Mexico
langs: Indigenous languages such as Nahuatl and Maya
known: Tacos, chilli and a food tradition recognised by UNESCO
Maya and Aztec ruins such as Chichén Itzá and Teotihuacán
Day of the Dead
Making cars, electronics and other goods for export to the United States
facts: The country with the most Spanish speakers in the world.
Mexico City is built on the site of the Aztec capital, Tenochtitlan.
It shares a border of about 3,100 kilometres with the United States, its biggest trading partner.

name: United States
known: Technology companies and Silicon Valley
Hollywood films, music and sport
Leading research universities
National parks such as Yellowstone and the Grand Canyon
facts: It is a federation of 50 states and the District of Columbia, and declared independence in 1776.
The world's largest economy, and the third most populous country.
English is the official language under a 2025 executive order, though federal law long had none and many languages are spoken.
